draft.title: World trade and health
card: Global trade is the movement of goods, services and money between countries. It can lift incomes and give people access to more products.
Trade also carries the marketing of products that harm health, such as tobacco, e-cigarettes and processed foods high in sugar, salt and unhealthy fat.
As these products become cheaper and easier to get, more people use or eat them. This can raise rates of chronic disease, such as heart disease, type 2 diabetes and some cancers.
Low and middle income countries are often targeted as markets grow. They may have weaker rules on advertising, and health systems that struggle with the extra burden of chronic disease.
draft.remember: Trade spreads harmful products and their marketing, which can raise chronic disease.

a.q: How can global trade lead to more chronic disease in a country?
opts: It spreads marketing of harmful products across borders
It spreads infectious disease between travellers
It lowers incomes so people cannot afford health care
It forces governments to close their local health services
a.why: Trade carries tobacco, e-cigarettes and processed foods and the marketing for them, so more people use them, and chronic disease can rise. Spread of infectious disease is a different pathway and is not the link taught here.
a.clue: Think about what products and advertising cross borders.

b.q: A fast food company based overseas opens outlets across a middle income country and advertises heavily to children. Which health effect is most likely to follow over time?
opts: A rise in type 2 diabetes and heart disease
A fall in rates of chronic disease from higher incomes
A rise in injuries from violence in the country
A fall in the use of processed foods
b.why: Trade brings cheap processed food and its marketing, so more people eat it, and chronic diseases such as type 2 diabetes and heart disease can rise. Higher incomes from trade can help, but the card links this marketing to more chronic disease, not less.
b.clue: Consider what the advertised food is high in and what disease it is linked to.

a.best: It spreads marketing of harmful products across borders

b.best: A rise in type 2 diabetes and heart disease
